summary: The note profiles the Silver Minds Project, a community-based mental health initiative for aging adults launched in October 2023, through the stories of several seniors. It covers depression, isolation, trauma, mental exercises, nutrition, technology and education, and stresses the role of family, friends and caregivers. The overall message is hope: with community support, seniors can overcome mental health struggles and keep cognitive sharpness.
one_line: Stories of seniors show how the Silver Minds Project uses social, mental, nutritional, technological and educational support to improve mental health and cognition in aging adults.
key_facts: New geriatric health initiatives began to take effect on September 1, 2023.

Dr. Eduardo Sanchez, a geriatric psychiatrist, spoke at the October 2023 inauguration of the Silver Minds Project and said "Mental health in our seniors is not just an individual concern, it's a growing public health issue."

The Silver Minds Project is a community-based mental health initiative whose mission is to promote mental well-being and enhance cognitive function among the elderly through therapeutic social activities, mental fitness exercises, and support networks.
78-year-old Martha Jensen does crossword puzzles daily and joined a local senior community center, an offshoot of the Silver Minds Project, where she attended group therapy sessions.
Martha Jensen met Linda McGinnis, a volunteer coordinator and retired nurse, at the community center, and McGinnis became a cherished confidante.
80-year-old Michael Thomson experienced depression and anxiety after his wife died and he retired; a neighbor noticed his withdrawal and suggested he speak to someone.
85-year-old George Kwan, a former college professor, leads a weekly book club at the senior gatherings.
79-year-old Anita Rodriguez found healing in a trauma-informed yoga class run by the Silver Minds Project, which uses mindfulness and gentle movement.
Nutritionist Dr. Vivian Lee stresses the role of diet and physical health in cognitive function, and the project offers nutritional workshops and exercise regimens for varying mobility levels.
77-year-old Jim Barnes adopted a Mediterranean diet and a daily walking group, which cleared what he calls "the mental fog."
82-year-old Emma Richardson lives in a remote area and uses telehealth for mental health check-ins; technology literacy classes teach her to use smartphones and computers.
74-year-old former teacher Helen Black leads mental health awareness workshops for seniors, supporting early recognition of cognitive decline and mental health issues.
